title: Closed-point coherent witness and invariance under an invertible twist
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\xi$ be its generic point, so $\overline{\{\xi\}}=C$, and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $z\ne\xi$ be a closed point, meaning $\{z\}$ is closed, and let $i:Z=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\hookrightarrow C$ be the canonical closed immersion [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-residue-field]. Let $\mathcal G=i_*\mathcal O_Z$, where the pushforward is the sheaf with $\mathcal G(U)=\mathcal O_Z(i^{-1}U)$ and $\mathcal O_C(U)$-action through the structure map. Then $\mathcal G$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent], its support $\{x:\mathcal G_x\ne0\}$ is $\{z\}$ and has dimension zero, and its stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] satisfy
$$\mathcal G_z\cong\kappa(z),\qquad \mathfrak m_z\mathcal G_z=0,\qquad \dim_{\kappa(z)}\mathcal G_z=1,\qquad\mathcal G_\xi=0.$$
The isomorphism at $z$ is $\mathcal O_{C,z}$-linear for the residue-map action on $\kappa(z)$, and dimension means [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Both tensors $\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal L\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}\mathcal G$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] are coherent, and their Euler characteristics [def-pc-euler-characteristic] satisfy
$$\chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal G)=\chi(C,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)=\chi(C,\mathcal G).$$

proof.text: Properness includes finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. A field is Noetherian: its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal, generated by zero and one. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$ are locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ to obtain that $C$ is locally Noetherian. The module $\mathcal O_Z$ is quasi-coherent (on its single affine chart it is the associated module of $\kappa(z)$) and is generated by $1$. Hence [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes $\mathcal O_Z$ coherent.

By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], the given closed immersion $i$ is finite. Its target $C$ is locally Noetherian by step 1 and its source module $\mathcal O_Z$ is coherent by that step. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent] applies and proves that $\mathcal G=i_*\mathcal O_Z$ is coherent.

The one point $t$ of $Z$ maps to $z$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)=\kappa(z)$, and $Z$ is the only neighbourhood of $t$, so the stalk definition [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] gives $\mathcal O_{Z,t}=\kappa(z)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks] to $i$: it identifies $\mathcal G_z$ with this field, linearly for the canonical stalk map $\mathcal O_{C,z}\to\kappa(z)$, and gives $\mathcal G_x=0$ for every $x\ne z$. This stalk map is the residue quotient of [def-weil-residue-field], because $i$ is the canonical residue-field immersion in the hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 00AE, lemma-stalks-closed-pushforward; module linearity as in Modules Tag 08KS, lemma-i-star-equivalence.

proof.text: Under step 3's linear identification, every $a\in\mathfrak m_z$ acts as its zero residue, so $\mathfrak m_z\mathcal G_z=0$. The element corresponding to $1\in\kappa(z)$ is a basis over $\kappa(z)$: every vector is a unique scalar multiple of it. Thus $\dim_{\kappa(z)}\mathcal G_z=1$ by [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], and this stalk is nonzero. All other stalks vanish by step 3, including $\mathcal G_\xi$ because $z\ne\xi$. The support is therefore exactly $\{z\}$. A singleton has exactly one nonempty irreducible closed subset and no strict inclusion between such subsets; its Krull dimension is zero by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Tag 0AYV, lemma-degree-on-proper-curve, proof of condition (2): the closed-point witness has generic rank zero.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support] with $X=C$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal N=\mathcal L$. Properness is a hypothesis, coherence is step 2, and the zero-dimensional support is step 4. Its third conclusion gives coherence of $\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L$ and $\chi(C,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)=\chi(C,\mathcal G)$.

source.place: Tag 0AYT, lemma-chi-tensor-finite, part (5), rank n=1; used in Tag 0AYV, lemma-degree-on-proper-curve.

proof.text: On the sectionwise balanced tensors defining [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the maps $g\otimes l\mapsto l\otimes g$ and $l\otimes g\mapsto g\otimes l$ respect balancing, commute with restriction and are inverse. Sheafifying them gives an $\mathcal O_C$-linear isomorphism $\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L\cong\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal G$. Coherence transfers across it: compose any finite free presentation map with the isomorphism, which identifies the kernels. Its induced maps on each cohomology group are inverse $k$-linear maps, so the dimensions in [def-pc-euler-characteristic] agree term by term. Together with step 5 this gives both asserted coherence statements and both Euler-characteristic equalities.
